verifications.note: Verified on candidate sha256:56415aeea66a2aa11e721024ff0d3a2c0321f629f5e41fb2cc0c95c2c392d1b3 (source cde60365) in a disposable, complete clone with a disposable PostgreSQL, Node 22.22.0, LANG unset; all data SYNTHETIC. This entry also covers my interrupted round-9 observation 600 (the digest read is not redacted). It has no finding id of its own, and it is the same defect class: D-226 says 'every response that serializes a notification'. (1) I re-ran my round-8 reproduction zz-cs-r8-inbox-text.test.ts unchanged (log 42): 5/5 pass. P1 uses the real producer's Finance-validation shape: tl2 gets 404 on benefit B01 and on its Finance validation. GET /me/work-items, GET /me/inbox and POST /me/inbox/{id}/read all return inbox.restricted, params {}, the transformation home link and the marker, with 'P1 leaks (0)'. P1b uses the real POST /benefit-overlaps producer: the Finance recipient's inbox is redacted, with 'P1b leaks (0)'. P1c (a benefit-route notification): the list and mark-read are redacted. (2) I re-ran my round-9 digest probe unchanged (log 45, renamed zz-cs-r10-digest.test.ts). The real worker job runDigestWindow digests tl2's held notification. GET /me/notification-digests/{id} now returns the item as messageKey inbox.restricted, params {} and the home link, with 'leaks (0)'. In round 9 this probe failed, naming the hidden ids and the code B01. (3) In-tree tests, unmutated: inbox-restricted-z13, digest-restricted-z14 and the tokens z13/z14 pass 27/27 (log 59). The notification-serializer sweep and the editor tests pass (log 59-unit). The full integration suite passes in both locales (logs 30, 31, 32). (4) Mutants, each caught by assertions: M1, the digest decision is computed but not applied: digest-restricted-z14 and my digest probe fail, 2 of 6 (log 50). M4, markInboxNotificationRead is no longer redacted: inbox-restricted-z13 and my round-8 probe fail, 3 of 12 (log 53). M6, a new API module serializes NotificationDigestItem from inbox_notification without the helpers: the serializer sweep fails (log 55). M6B, the helper names are kept but shadowed by no-ops: the textual sweep passes, as I expected (it is a name heuristic), but digest-restricted-z14 fails (log 57). So a functional regression is caught even where the heuristic is fooled. (5) Source: every API module that reads inbox_notification is either in the sweep or listed with a reason (60-source-checks.log). The worker's channel fan-out applies the twin decision (restrictedForRecipient). The digest notification itself carries only {count}.
